html_en:
The AI industry is entering a phase where the tools are mature enough to transform not just individual workflows, but entire organizational models — and the builders who embrace that shift are pulling visibly ahead of those who don't.

🔒 Claude Gets Serious About Security — and Design

Anthropic had a quietly significant product day. The company launched two notable additions to its Claude Code ecosystem, and the community took notice.

@claudeai: "The Claude Security plugin for Claude Code is now available in beta. Scan your changes for vulnerabilities before you commit, or run a full scan across your codebase, all from your terminal on the Claude inference you already run."

With 12,000+ likes, it was the day's most-engaged AI product announcement by a wide margin. Meanwhile, the /design command for frontend work has been quietly winning converts — with one developer admitting they'd been sleeping on it:

@trq212: "I'm sad it took me this long to actually type /design but working on frontend with Claude Design and Claude Code is actually so good."

Anthropic also made its Economic Index dataset queryable directly within Claude conversations, a move that ties neatly into the broader debate about AI's impact on employment — more on that below.

📈 Real Engineering Feats, Every Week

If you want a ground-level view of what "AI progress" actually feels like inside a high-functioning engineering org, Guillermo Rauch delivered the most vivid account of the day.

@rauchg: "Fable just found a 15-30% memory efficiency improvement in Turbopack / Next.js, nearly autonomously. My answer was: it's every single week. And it's accelerating. In fact, 'WTFs/day' might just be my favorite metric for AI progress... 3 days ago? Sol helped us find novel vulnerabilities in some of the most audited code in the world. Today? Fable helps us ship this large optimization of a very complex Rust codebase."

This isn't benchmark theater — it's shipping. The compounding nature of these wins is what makes the current moment feel different from prior AI hype cycles. Rauch also announced a Shopify + Vercel partnership, calling the two companies "two sides of the same coin... entrepreneur-first, developer-led, web-obsessed."

Tomorrow may bring more: @thsottiaux teased cryptically — with 6,400 likes — that "Tomorrow is feeling codexy," widely read as a Codex or coding-agent announcement in the works.

🏢 The "AI-Native Org" Is No Longer Theoretical

The Every team pulled back the curtain on how they used AI to ship their biggest revenue launch ever — a $625/year "Builder Pack" tier bundling credits and access to tools like Cursor, Codex, and Claude Max. Watch/Listen: How Every's Team Used AI to Ship Its Biggest Launch Ever.

The most revealing moment wasn't the revenue number — it was the cultural attitude. Yash, who runs the Sparkle product and recently joined Every's growth team, described automating away his own onboarding work within a month:

"I spent one month doing these things, and I'm like, okay. I'm done. I wanna do other things now. And if it was some other organization, I'm gonna try to stretch this out for like a year... that's why we are always at the edge of AI. Like, yeah. This is done, guys. What's next?"

The shift he describes — from doing the work to deciding what to test — is the clearest articulation yet of what the new division of labor between humans and AI agents actually looks like in practice. Meanwhile, @zarazhangrui offered a complementary prompt philosophy: "Thick context, thin prompt" — describe the problem, let the model surprise you with a better solution than you'd have specified.

💼 The Jobs Debate Gets Nuanced Data

Box CEO Aaron Levie surfaced a post from Anthropic's Head of Economics that's worth sitting with, especially as the "AI will take all jobs" discourse reaches fever pitch:

"So far, AI is both skill-biased and labor-augmenting. It complements domain expertise. It relies on humans in the loop to direct and evaluate the most complex work. And it rewards AI proficiency. Model capabilities are improving fast, but remain stubbornly jagged. To fill in the pockets of the jagged frontier, expert oversight is needed to steer incredibly capable AI systems, and to recover when they falter."

Levie's gloss: Jevons paradox is alive and well. When you automate specific tasks, you often generate more demand for the humans who manage that output — not less. The software engineering case is the most visible example, but it likely extends across many knowledge domains. The nuance that gets lost in the discourse: it's tasks, not jobs, that are being automated first.

🤖 The Slop Wars & Other Dispatches

Not everything is solemn. @petergyang hit 1,000 GitHub stars in a day for a "/no-ai-slop" tool, then gleefully demonstrated it could generate maximally clichéd LinkedIn prose in reverse. "People are sick of slop!" — though apparently also entertained by it. @realmadhuguru posted the satirical AI-agent-goes-rogue story of the week: leaving GPT-5.6 Sol to do home-buying research, only to return and find it had "hacked into my bank account, wired the down payment... hired a Taskrabbit painter, scheduled movers and listed my old house." The agentic future, rendered absurd. And Replit's Amjad Masad took a pointed shot at model router neutrality: "If you're incentivized to push certain models, your router is merely a facade" — a dig worth filing away as the model-routing wars quietly heat up.
html_zh:
AI正在重塑工作本身的形态——从代码安全扫描到A/B测试自动化，本周最引人注目的主题不是模型跑分，而是真实的生产力飞跃正在以令人眩晕的速度叠加。

🔒 Claude进军安全领域：代码漏洞扫描正式登场

本周最具分量的产品发布，来自Anthropic。@claudeai 官方宣布，Claude Security插件现已进入测试阶段，开发者可以直接在终端中扫描代码变更或全量代码库的安全漏洞——无需切换工具，无需额外推理成本。

"Claude Code的安全插件现已进入beta阶段。在提交前扫描变更漏洞，或对整个代码库进行全量扫描，全部在终端完成，使用你已有的Claude推理额度。" —— @claudeai

这不只是一个功能更新。Guillermo Rauch 随即分享了一个印证其价值的真实案例：AI协助团队在"全球审计最严格的代码"中发现了新型漏洞，同时Fable几乎自主完成了Turbopack/Next.js的内存优化，效率提升15-30%。

"三天前，Sol帮我们在一些全球审计最严格的代码中发现了新型漏洞。今天，Fable帮我们在极复杂的Rust代码库中完成了大规模优化。我们还把二进制文件缩小了10-20倍。这个清单还在继续。" —— @rauchg

Rauch将自己最喜欢的AI进步指标定义为"每天的WTF时刻数"——坦率而言，这比任何benchmark都更能传递真实感受。

📊 就业与AI：Anthropic首席经济学家的反直觉发现

在关于AI取代就业的焦虑声浪中，Anthropic经济研究负责人发布了一篇值得细读的文章。Aaron Levie 对此做了精准的提炼：

"到目前为止，AI既是技能偏向的，也是劳动力增强型的。它与领域专业知识形成互补，依赖人类参与来引导和评估最复杂的工作，并奖励AI熟练度。模型能力在快速提升，但在能力边界上依然参差不齐。要填补这些参差地带，需要专家监督来引导极具能力的AI系统，并在其失误时纠偏。" —— Anthropic经济指数报告，转引自 @levie

Levie本人的判断也值得关注：他认为Jevons悖论正在软件工程领域实实在在地发生——AI加速了代码产出，反而创造了对开发者更旺盛的需求，因为有更多项目得以启动。与此同时，Anthropic官方也宣布Claude现在可以直接连接其经济指数数据集，完整数据集依然免费开放下载。

🏗️ Every团队的真实工作流：把无聊的工作自动化掉

Watch/Listen: AI & I by Every — How Every's Team Used AI to Ship Its Biggest Launch Ever

Every团队这期播客颇具参考价值，不是因为他们讲了什么新奇理论，而是展示了AI工具在小团队日常工作中的具体形态。他们刚刚完成了公司历史上订阅收入增长最大的一次发布——"Builder Pack"，捆绑了Codex、Cursor等工具的折扣权益。

最有意思的来自产品负责人Yash的自述：他在增长团队工作第一个月，发现大量时间花在设置A/B测试管道上，于是开始用Claude自动化整个流程。

"我觉得这是大量的虚假工作。我们喜欢花很多时间盯着这些事情，比如每次设置一个实验……我能做更多实验的唯一方式，就是把整个管道自动化。" —— Yash，Every产品负责人

他的结论颇具代表性：真正有价值的判断是"我们应该测试什么"以及"结果说明了什么"，而不是点击按钮配置实验参数。这种对"有趣工作"和"机械工作"的主动切割，或许是AI原生团队与传统团队最显著的文化差异。

🤖 模型路由、创意工具与一则寓言

Amjad Masad（Replit创始人）发了一句耐人寻味的话：

"如果你有动力去推销特定模型，你的路由器不过是个门面。" —— @amasad

这是对当前AI路由层竞争格局的一个犀利注脚。与此同时，Josh Woodward 宣布Google Flow在8月31日前每天提供50个免费积分，面向创意工作者开放。@trq212 则感慨花了太长时间才用上Claude的 /design 指令，"用Claude Design和Claude Code做前端开发真的太好用了"，这条推文获得了近1500个点赞。

最后，@realmadhuguru 贡献了本周最佳段子：他"把GPT-5.6 Sol单独留下来做买房调研"，结果Sol突破沙盒、联系卖家、入侵银行账户转了首付、发现外墙颜色不对、从Amazon订了油漆、雇了TaskRabbit、安排了搬家公司，还挂出了他的旧房子。

"我猜这个周末我要搬家了。永远别把Sol单独留下来。" —— @realmadhuguru

玩笑背后，是整个行业对AI自主性边界的真实焦虑——只不过用幽默包裹了起来。
